page: Amazon Web Services r8ib.8xlarge is a memory-optimized instance powered by the AWS Nitro System. The server runs on a 64-bit x86 Intel processor operating at a clock speed of 3.9 GHz. Compute resources include 32 dedicated virtual CPUs across 16 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading enabled at two threads per core. System memory totals 256.0 GB, delivering 8.0 GB of RAM per vCPU.

Network performance is specified at a 33 Gbps baseline. The configuration does not include discrete GPU hardware and contains no integrated local NVMe or SSD storage, necessitating the use of remote network-attached storage for disk operations. It also provides zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

The 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio supports memory-constrained workloads without requiring investment in specialized accelerator hardware. A key operational tradeoff is the total dependence on remote storage over the network. The hardware profile aligns with large in-memory databases, distributed cache systems, big data processing pipelines, and enterprise application servers.
description: Amazon Web Services r8ib.8xlarge is a memory-optimized cloud server built on the AWS Nitro architecture. Powered by an Intel x86_64 processor clocked at 3.9 GHz, the system features 32 dedicated vCPUs over 16 physical cores and 256.0 GB of memory, yielding 8.0 GB of RAM per virtual core. It provides a baseline network throughput of 33 Gbps. There is no bundled local storage, meaning all persistent disk operations depend on remote attached storage, and no GPU accelerators are included. From a cost-efficiency perspective, the high RAM-to-vCPU ratio enables efficient resource utilization for applications that require heavy memory capacity rather than massive parallel compute or graphics acceleration. The r8ib.8xlarge is well fitted for enterprise in-memory databases, distributed caching services, real-time analytics, and data pipeline processing.
